claims.text: The test alloy is equimolar WTaTiVZr.
Equimolar WTaTiVZr can be synthesized as a single-phase, likely BCC alloy.
The WTaTiVZr alloy has inherent severe lattice distortion.
Refractory HEAs such as the proposed WTaTiVZr material typically possess a fine or moderately refined grain structure.
Severe lattice distortion creates a rough energy landscape in WTaTiVZr.
The rough energy landscape balances vacancy and self-interstitial mobilities.
Balanced point-defect mobilities promote dynamic dislocation recovery.
Lattice distortion and activated grain-boundary sites enhance grain-boundary-mediated plasticity at high temperature.
Mixed atomic species produce local lattice strain that disrupts conventional dislocation motion relative to pure tungsten.
Dynamic recombination and grain-boundary-mediated deformation produce more spatially distributed plastic flow.
Distributed plastic flow suppresses dislocation pile-up and premature crack initiation.
Under identical high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will have lower dislocation pile-up and greater dynamic recovery than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will have higher plastic strain to failure than pure tungsten.
Under identical high-temperature loading, WTaTiVZr will have greater fracture toughness than pure tungsten.
Deformed WTaTiVZr will exhibit wavy dislocation lines and active grain-boundary sliding that are absent in pure tungsten.
Pure tungsten typically has limited plasticity and brittle failure under the specified high-temperature loading because of dislocation pile-up and less active recovery.
The proposed mechanism is applicable over 800–1200°C and strain rates representative of sustained plasma-facing-component service.
The mechanism applies to conventionally processed WTaTiVZr microstructures having the requisite lattice distortion and grain structure.
The proposed comparison excludes effects from impurities and large-scale processing defects.
